h1: Aluminum & PVC upcut saws — automatic upcut, double-head, glazing bead and miter saws for extrusions and window profiles
intro: An upcut saw (rising-blade saw) raises its blade from under the table through a profile that is already clamped, so the cut is guarded, square and nearly burr-free — the standard saw for aluminum extrusions and PVC (vinyl) window profiles. NovoTech supplies the saws of Plastmak, built in Bursa, Turkey: the SÇ 401, whose Ø17-11/16″ blade turns from 0° to 180°; the fully automatic SÇ 402 and SÇ 403 with Ø21-5/8″ to Ø25-9/16″ blades and hydro-pneumatic feed, for profiles up to 9-3/16 × 12-3/8″; the SÇ 450 for roller-shutter boxes and lamella packs; the SÇ 400S and SÇ 4000S double-head saws, which cut both ends of a frame profile at once, up to 171-5/8″ long; the SÇ 301 and SÇ 301S glazing bead saws; and the SÇ 431, SÇ 441 and SÇ 451 miter saws. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON.

faq.a: A saw whose blade sits under the table and rises through the profile, which is clamped from above and from the side before the cut. The blade stays covered until it cuts, the profile cannot move, and the cut comes out square and nearly burr-free — which is why aluminum and PVC window shops use upcut saws rather than chop saws. The SÇ 401, SÇ 402 and SÇ 403 are upcut saws; the SÇ 431, 441 and 451 cut from above.

faq.q: Which blade size do I need?
faq.a: The blade decides the largest profile. At 90° the Ø17-11/16″ (450 mm) SÇ 401 cuts profiles up to 5-5/16″ high and 8-9/16″ wide, the Ø21-5/8″ (550 mm) SÇ 402 7-1/16 × 10-7/16″, and the SÇ 403 8-3/16 × 11-5/16″ with its Ø23-5/8″ (600 mm) blade or 9-3/16 × 12-3/8″ with the Ø25-9/16″ (650 mm) one. Most window and door profiles fit the SÇ 401 or 402; curtain-wall and large door profiles need the SÇ 403. Send us your largest profile and we will check it against the cutting chart.

An upcut saw cuts one end at a time — flexible and inexpensive, enough for a few dozen windows a shift. A double-head saw cuts both ends at once, to a length typed in or read from a barcode, with both heads tilting to 45°: the SÇ 400S and SÇ 4000S roughly double a shop's output and take measuring errors out of the job. Many shops run a double-head saw for frames and an upcut saw for mullions and odd cuts.

faq.q: Do they cut aluminum as well as PVC?
faq.a: Yes. The SÇ 402, 403, 400S and 4000S cut both, with hydro-pneumatic or hydro-check feeds that keep aluminum cuts clean and spray or oil cooling for the blade; the SÇ 401 slows its feed in aluminum and takes an optional cooling device and hydro-check. Fit a blade made for the material you cut.

faq.q: What do the model names mean?
faq.a: SÇ — often written SC — is Plastmak's model prefix. Across the range, 1xx are welders, 2xx end mills and notchers, 3xx bead saws, 4xx saws, 5xx routers and CNCs, 6xx corner cleaners, 9xx crimpers and 1000s conveyors; an S marks the servo or upgraded version, as on the SÇ 400S and SÇ 4000S.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
